relevance_note: A Japanese family in which affected members carry a heterozygous TNFAIP3 missense variant: 'the heterozygous C243Y mutation was present in all familial patients with BD examined'.
method_note: Read the full Markdown by hand; the paper has no data tables (patients are described in prose in 'Patients and family history'). A short Python script in my scratch directory assembled the JSON from values I transcribed while reading; spans were then checked verbatim against the paper by script. Labels: 'Patient 1'-'Patient 6' as in the text; the unaffected, genotyped sibling is 'healthy younger brother' (also called 'the healthy sibling' and 'her son'). No family label is given. Contradictions/uncertainties: (1) The abstract says 'all affected family members carried a heterozygous C243Y mutation', but Methods and Figure 1 say patient 6 was not sequenced; no variant row is given for Patient 6, and n_patients_reported=6 follows the authors' statement although only 5 were genotyped. (2) For Patient 6 the text says she 'suffered from recurrent oral and genital ulcers' and then 'A history of genital ulcers could not be ascertained.'; an observed phenotypic row is kept with both spans and the checklist item is 'not reported'. (3) Discussion on NLRP3 is internally inconsistent ('could not confirm the enhanced NLRP3 mRNA, but could confirm elevated NLRP3 mRNA levels in C243Y A20 THP-1 cells ... in patient 1'); only the Results statement on transfected THP-1 cells is used. Variant notes: the cDNA is printed as '728 G>A' without a 'c.' prefix or transcript, and the protein as 'C243Y' without 'p.'; both recorded exactly as printed. The genomic string 'chr6_138197226_G>A' has no build attached; Methods state alignment to 'Genome Reference Consortium human reference 37' but I did not join that to the value. A second TNFAIP3 change in Patient 1 ('three nucleotide deletions in an intron of upper exon 3', absent in the mother, origin not investigated) is recorded as its own row with type 'other'. CASP8AP2 and WIF1 are named only as genes in the filtered WES set without variant descriptions, so no rows. Inheritance is 'not reported' for every row: the mother (Patient 2) carries C243Y and the family is described as autosomal dominant, but no row states the parental origin explicitly (rule 8). Patient 3 is 'grandmother' without 'maternal'. Phenotype decisions: 'None of the patients had exhibited ocular lesions of BD' excludes ocular inflammation for Patients 1-6 as a named-group statement (not the brother). Patient 1's perianal ulcer was not mapped to genital or gastrointestinal checklist items. Patient 6's fever is recorded but 'recurrent fever' left 'not reported' (recurrence not stated). The brother's 'neither BD symptoms' is one excluded row; no specific checklist items were excluded from it. Patient 1's age 17 is age at referral (recorded as last evaluation); his age at clinical diagnosis is not stated. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null: the paper makes no statement either way.

functional_evidence_statement.value: Mononuclear cells of patients 1 and 2 produced large amounts of IL-1β, IL-6 and TNF-α on stimulation versus controls; C243Y-transfected THP-1 cells suppressed inflammatory cytokine secretion much less than wild-type; suppression of Nod2-mediated NF-κB activation by C243Y about two-thirds of wild-type (weak function rather than complete loss of function); C243Y-transfected THP-1 cells showed increased NLRP3 transcript on stimulation
span: Mononuclear cells obtained from the proband and his mother produced large amounts of interleukin 1β, IL-6 and tumour necrosis factor α (TNF-a) on stimulation as compared with those from normal controls.
Although inflammatory cytokine secretion was suppressed by wild-type transfected cells, it was suppressed to a much lesser extent by mutated C243Y A20/TNFAIP3-transfected cells.
the suppression of NF-κB activation by C243Y A20 was approximately two-thirds that of intact A20
This finding indicates that the A20 variant possessing the C243Y mutation should be regarded as a variant that does not cause complete loss of function, but, rather, causes weak function.
